chapter_title: The Chapter of the Four Kingdoms
chapter_note: This chapter is essentially a homiletic/pastoral exhortation built around a Gospel saying about giving bread and water, extended to Manichaean institutional categories (disciple/saints/catechumen) and reward-at-the-last-day logic. It contains no systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping or impersonal cosmological mechanics characteristic of the oldest teaching substrate; the second half shows strong pastoral drift (alms, fellowship, catechumens, blessing/exhortation).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening and dialogue attribution: "Once again the apostle speaks" is a classic hagiographic/compilation frame marker; not part of the old substrate.
World-anchored political catalogue (Babylon/Persia, Romans, Axumites, Silis) used as sermonic setup; not a cosmos→cosmos mapping and not part of the impersonal cosmological substrate.

Paraphrastic Gospel-style saying (bread + cup of water given to a disciple “in truth”) with strong direct-address/application voice; the content belongs to the Jesus-saying tradition entering via Christian overlay rather than the pre-compilation cosmological substrate.

Institutional extension of the charity saying to a "catechumen of the truth" and promise of eternal rest; this is church-level categorization and reward exhortation rather than core cosmological exposition.
Explicit citation formula: "Just as the saying that the good saviour uttered" followed by the bread/water saying—material entering via Gospel tradition (NT overlay).

paragraphs.removed_material: Although the paragraph moves from interpreting the saviour’s phrase (“least of the faithful”) to institutional application about catechumens and moral critique of kingdoms, none of its clauses exhibit the impersonal, systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential substrate; it is an interpretive/application composition built on NT overlay plus institutional pastoral extension.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Interpretation of a Jesus-saying plus explicit institutional application (“catechumens… fellowship… helps them”); the paragraph is composite in sources (Gospel overlay + pastoral), but contains no recoverable ancient cosmological substrate to extract.

Indwelling "Holy Spirit" in named community types (faithful catechumen / faithful righteous one) with direct address (“I tell you”) reflects Christianized doctrinal/application language rather than the old cosmological substrate.

Alms/fellowship motivation and reward logic (“last day”) framed around the Holy Spirit dwelling in saints; operational piety and recompense discourse indicates later pastoral catechesis rather than substrate teaching.
Exhortative blessing and appeal to hear/believe/set the heart; application voice without cosmological mechanism—typical sermonic/pastoral conclusion.
